units.text: Question: The third question in the letter of Brother Salih Abduh Al-Yamani from the city of Al-Khobar, he says: What is the meaning of the testimony that there is no god but Allah, and what is the meaning of the testimony that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, please benefit us, may Allah reward you?

Answer: These two testimonies are the foundation of Islam, and they are the basis of the religion. By them the disbeliever who does not utter them enters Islam, by them he enters Islam and is counted among the people of Islam, and is required to fulfill the rest of the rights of Islam.
As for the testimony that there is no god but Allah, it is the basis of the religion and the foundation of faith in all religions, all the religions of the messengers, from Adam to our present day. Adam (peace and blessings be upon him) came with it, and the messengers came with it, such as Noah, Hud, Salih, Ibrahim and others among the messengers. All of them called the nations to this word. Allah, the Most High, said: ⟦Q1⟧ [An-Nahl:36]. Allah, the Most High, said: ⟦Q2⟧ [Al-Anbiya:25]. And our Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, when Allah sent him, began with his people with this, saying to them: "Say: there is no god but Allah, and you will succeed." When they were worshipping idols and trees, and they had many gods around the Ka'bah and elsewhere, they rejected this and said: ⟦Q3⟧ [Sad:5]. They rejected monotheism and faith due to their ignorance and disbelief and misguidance and their habituation to what their forefathers were upon of polytheism, disbelief and worship of many gods.
This word is the best branch of faith, as in the Sahih from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "Faith has seventy-some branches—or he said—sixty-some branches, the best of which is saying: there is no god but Allah, and the least of which is removing harm from the road, and modesty is a branch of faith." This great hadith shows us that the origin of the religion, the foundation of the creed and the best of speech is saying: there is no god but Allah. Its meaning is: there is no true deity worthy of worship except Allah. It negates divinity—that is, worship—from other than Allah, and affirms it for Allah alone, glorified and exalted be He.
And in ... the Sahih from Sahih Muslim .. from Ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both), from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "Islam is built on five: on the oneness of Allah, establishment of prayer, giving zakah, fasting Ramadan, and pilgrimage to the House." And in another wording: "on that Allah alone is worshipped and disbelief in what is besides Him." So He made the oneness of Allah, worshipping Him alone and disbelief in what is besides Him as the meaning of: there is no god but Allah. In the two Sahihs from the hadith of Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him), in the question of Jibril, that when he asked the Messenger about Islam, he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Islam is to worship Allah and not associate anything with Him, and to establish prayer..." to the end. So He made worshipping Allah alone and not associating anything with Him as the meaning of there is no god but Allah. This is its meaning: affirming worship for Allah alone, singling Him out for it, glorified and exalted be He, apart from everything else, and believing in the invalidity of it for other than Him, glorified be He. Allah, the Most High, said: ⟦Q4⟧ [Al-Hajj:62]. This is the meaning of there is no god but Allah: affirming worship for Allah alone, which is divinity, and negating it from other than Him. So no one is called upon except Allah alone, no help is sought except from Him, no reliance is placed except upon Him, no prayer is performed except to Him, no vow is made except to Him, and no sacrifice is made except for Him, and so on.
By this you know—O questioner and O noble listener—you know that what some ignorant people do at some graves and with some awliya' (saints) of seeking help from the dead, calling upon the dead, calling upon trees and stones, or calling upon idols and seeking help from them, this is major polytheism (shirk), and it contradicts the saying: there is no god but Allah.
As for the testimony that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, its meaning is: belief that he is truly the Messenger of Allah, and that Allah sent him to the two heavy species, the jinn and mankind, as a bearer of good news and a warner, peace and blessings be upon him, and that he is the seal of the prophets, no prophet after him, as Allah, the Majestic and Most High, said: ⟦Q5⟧ [Al-Ahzab:40]. And He, the Most High, said: ⟦Q6⟧ [Al-Ahzab:45-46]. So he is truly the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him; Allah sent him to all people—their jinn and their humans—calling them to the oneness of Allah and warning them against associating partners with Allah, as the Mighty and Majestic said: ⟦Q7⟧ [Al-A'raf:158]. Allah, the Most High, said: ⟦Q8⟧ [Saba:28].
So every Muslim man and every Muslim woman, indeed every person, must believe that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. It is obligatory upon all those who are accountable, from Muslims, Jews, Christians and others, all accountable people must testify that there is no god but Allah, single out Allah for worship, abandon worship of anything besides Him, such as idols, trees, stones, prophets, awliya' and others. They must believe that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, believe that he is truly the Messenger of Allah, that he is the seal of the prophets, and that it is obligatory to follow him; that is by believing in what he came with, believing that he is truly the Messenger of Allah, obeying his commands, avoiding his prohibitions, and not worshipping Allah except with his legislation, peace and blessings be upon him. This is the meaning of this testimony, the testimony that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah: believing him in what he reported, obeying him in what he commanded, avoiding what he forbade and prohibited, peace and blessings be upon him, and not worshipping Allah except with his legislation that he came with, peace and blessings be upon him, not by whims, opinions or innovations. This is the meaning of the testimony that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.
These two testimonies—as previously mentioned—are the foundation of the religion and the basis of the creed. Whoever utters them and believes their meaning is a Muslim, and he must perform the rest of the obligations, such as prayer, zakah, fasting, Hajj and other things that Allah and His Messenger commanded. He must also avoid what Allah and His Messenger forbade, such as adultery, theft, disobedience to parents and all other forbidden things. Also, he must avoid major polytheism which is the opposite of monotheism. He must avoid major polytheism, for his monotheism will not be complete except by that. He must avoid all that Allah and His Messenger forbade of statements and actions in realization of these two testimonies. And Allah is the Guardian of success.
Presenter: May Allah be good to you.
